injuries.detail: Adams was placed on IR in early October and missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in all three of Arizona's practices this week. Now that he's been activated, Adams is eligible to suit up Sunday, and if he returns he'll likely reclaim his starting role at right guard.

Bowman was previously elevated for Week 6, when he logged four snaps on special teams (and none on offense) against the Rams. His usage could be similarly limited Sunday against Seattle, as the Cardinals have three healthy tight ends (Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano) ahead of Bowman in the pecking order.

Ford signed with Arizona's practice squad Oct. 14 and is now set to potentially make his gameday debut with the team Sunday in Seattle. He spent his first four NFL campaigns with Cleveland and averaged an acceptable 4.3 yards per carry with seven rushing touchdowns over 340 totes while also accumulating 647 yards and an additional five touchdowns on 107 catches across 57 games. Given that level of experience, it will be interesting to see how much the Cardinals utilize Ford on Sunday, though Tyler Allgeier is slated to work as the team's lead back, and Evan Hull will also factor into the mix.

Gaines continues to battle a knee injury and will miss his third straight game. Hayden Conner may make another start at right guard, though Isaiah Adams (ankle) -- who has been deemed questionable -- could take on that role if he's activated from IR on Saturday.

Williams made an early exit from Sunday's loss to Dallas after hurting his knee. He didn't practice at all this week and is set to miss the first game of his career. The rookie has started four of Arizona's first eight contests of the campaign.

An ankle injury caused Nolen to miss Arizona's past two contests, but he was able to log a trio of limited practices this week. That gives him at least a chance of suiting up Sunday in Seattle. Should Nolen need to sit out again, though, L.J. Collier could soak up most of his defensive snaps.

Melton missed Week 7 versus Denver due to a knee issue but was able to return last Sunday against Dallas. However, the injury is still a concern, and the third-year cornerback was limited in practice both Thursday and Friday this week. If he can't play in Week 9, Kalen King may log a start.

Wilson has worn a yellow non-contact jersey in practice the last two weeks due to two broken ribs -- a situation that contained him to limited sessions. Having said that, he'll continue to play through the concern as he did this past Sunday in Dallas, when he hauled in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown while adding one carry for 17 yards on a 79 percent snap share.

After being concussed early in last Sunday's game against Dallas, Knight will miss at least one contest, as he remains in the league's protocol. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) also sidelined, Tyler Allgeier projects to handle most of the backfield work, though it's a really tough road draw against a strong run defense.

Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.

Virgil played a season-high 38 offensive snaps, but he went without a reception for the third straight week. The Cardinals placed Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) on injured reserve Tuesday after the wide receiver fractured his right tibia in Week 8, so more opportunities could come Virgil's way moving forward. Regardless of an increase in workload, the team's Week 9 matchup versus Seattle will be a challenging one for the 22-year-old.

Duvernay reeled in his first two passes of the year while playing 34 offensive snaps in the victory. Fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) fractured his right tibia during the contest, and he is likely set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.

Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.

Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.

After previously leading the Cardinals backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, Allgeier is now slated for a longer run atop the depth chart while Love is projected to miss 4-to-5 weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain. Love sustained his latest ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys, with his early exit clearing the way for Allgeier to run wild. Allgeier finished with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight sustained a concussion and is uncertain to play Week 9 against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substantial success in Week 8, he came into the contest averaging just 2.9 yards per carry on 61 totes. He'll also be facing a Seattle defense that is tied for the second-fewest yards per carry (3.8) allowed to running backs this season, so a repeat performance by Allgeier would be surprising.

Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.

Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.

Though Bourne is expected to avoid surgery after fracturing his right tibia during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys, he's facing an expected recovery timeline of three months that effectively ends his season. With Bourne heading to IR, the Cardinals signed Harrison Wallace off their practice squad to replenish their depth at receiver. The 31-year-old Bourne will finish the 2026 campaign with 26 receptions for 263 yards and no touchdowns on 38 targets over eight appearances.

Ryland's missed PAT came in the fourth quarter with 1:03 remaining after Michael Wilson's touchdown knotted the game at 30-30. Arizona was lucky to get to overtime, but Ryland made the winning kick with 4:09 remaining, drilling a 42-yard field goal. On the season, he's made 19 of 21 field-goal tries and 16 of 17 extra-point attempts.

Beck had been a healthy inactive through each of the Cardinals' first eight games of the season as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, but he'll get the chance to dress for the first time in Week 9 after Arizona removed the struggling Jacoby Brissett from the starting role and dropped him down two spots on the depth chart. Like Brissett, the 30-year-old Minshew is a journeyman who isn't viewed as the team's long-term solution under center, so it wouldn't be surprising if Beck eventually received a look as the starter before the end of the season if Arizona eventually fades from playoff contention. A rookie third-round pick out of Miami, Beck completed 15 of 19 pass attempts for 188 yards and a touchdown during his lone preseason appearance.

Unsurprisingly, the Cardinals have opted to appoint Minshew to the top spot on the depth chart after he came on in relief of a struggling Jacoby Brissett and led a stirring comeback in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys. In what was his first appearance of the season, Minshew completed 17 of 23 pass attempts for 188 yards and three touchdowns in just under two quarters' worth of action before Chad Ryland sealed the victory with a walk-off 42-yard field goal. Though his performance in future games will ultimately dictate how long he sticks around as the Cardinals' starter, Minshew is far from a lock to hold down the job for the balance of the season. If the 3-5 Cardinals eventually fade from playoff contention, LaFleur may want to give an extended look to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will serve as Minshew's top backup in Week 9 while Brissett falls to third on the depth chart, per Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site.

Zaccheaus was pulled from the game in the third quarter to be evaluated for a concussion. He cleared protocol relatively quickly and returned during the same period. He'll try to help Atlanta's offense rally back from a fourth-quarter deficit.

Bowman practiced fully all week and was eligible to return from a two-game absence with a hamstring injury, but per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, he was left off the roster "not for an injury or performance reason" but rather because of a "numbers game" involving other healthy players.
As was the case in Week 8, Dalton will not occupy a roster spot Sunday, but he will be permitted to play should both Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa be forced from the game and unable to return.

Abdullah was placed on injured reserve Oct. 10 due to a hamstring injury, and after missing the required four games while on the list, he was designated to return Wednesday and then activated Saturday, setting him up for his first game action since Week 4. A rotational role off the edge is likely for Abdullah due to James Pearce (back) making his season debut and all of Cameron Thomas, Za'Darius Smith and Charles Snowden available to the defense.

Pearce completed his eight-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy this week, but after being listed as a full participant on the Falcons' first two Week 9 injury reports, he was limited by a back injury Friday and thus entered the weekend as questionable to play. With his status now clarified for Sunday's matchup, he seems likely to resume his role as one of Atlanta's top pass rushers, which equated to 10.5 sacks among his 26 tackles in 17 regular-season games as a first-round rookie in 2025.

Since suffering a forearm injury during a Week 6 loss to the Bears, Deablo has missed the last two contests, and while he capped Week 9 prep with a questionable designation, his full session Friday signaled that he was closing in on a return to action. With that confirmed, he's a good bet to retake one of the starting inside linebacker spots in the Falcons defense, despite Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins holding down the fort in Deablo's absence.

On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

injuries.evidence: If Atlanta doesn't activate Williams by next Thursday, he'll be required to miss the remainder of the campaign.
injuries.detail: Williams was designated to return to practice Oct. 22 and logged a trio of full practices this week. However, the Falcons have elected against activating him ahead of Sunday's game. If Atlanta doesn't activate Williams by next Thursday, he'll be required to miss the remainder of the campaign.

Herbert was elevated for both Week 7 and Week 8, turning six carries into 21 yards and two catches (on two targets) into 22 yards while also working as a kick returner. He could take on a bigger role Sunday versus Cincinnati and potentially beyond, as No. 2 RB Brian Robinson was placed on injured reserve Saturday due to a hamstring injury. That means Herbert is the Falcons' only healthy running back behind workhorse Bijan Robinson

Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.

The kicker missed wide left from 53 yards out in the first quarter. It was difficult for the Atlanta offense to move the ball in rainy conditions. Folk has failed to connect on four of 16 field-goal tries and one of 16 extra points in 2026.

Blair has been active for all eight of the Falcons' games this season, but the 29-year-old wideout has been scarcely involved on offense. He's thus far recorded just a six-yard reception on four targets, three of which came in Week 2. Blair should continue to suit up for the Falcons on gamedays but will provide most of his value on special teams.

Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

Pitts was unable to make it four straight weeks with a touchdown, and he was held to two or fewer catches for the first time since Week 3 versus Green Bay. The tight end has exceeded 50 receiving yards just one time over eight contests to open the 2026 campaign, so fantasy managers are pretty reliant on him reaching the end zone. Pitts and the rest of the Falcons' offense will have a good chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Bengals' inconsistent defense.

Penix endured a career-worst all-around game in rainy conditions after coming into the afternoon with just one interception in his first five games. Only two of Penix's four picks led to Buccaneers points -- and just a pair of field goals at that -- but the Falcons defense was helpless against Tampa Bay's ground attack in the shutout. Sunday's conditions were a clear outlier, so Penix should be expected to bounce back across the pond in a Week 9 matchup against a vulnerable Bengals secondary next Sunday in Madrid.

Michael Penix was picked off four times by the Buccaneers' defense throughout the rainy afternoon while completing only 33.3 percent of his passes, so London's near career-worst numbers were a bit more understandable in that context. The talented wideout had come into the day with at least 62 receiving yards in five straight contests, and he should have a chance to bounce back when the Falcons face off with the Bengals in Madrid next Sunday.

It was a bizarre afternoon overall in very rainy conditions in Tampa Bay, and Robinson managed to salvage his day with a solid rushing yardage total. Robinson's tally on the ground was actually his best since Week 5, although his streak of games without a rushing touchdown extended to four. Robinson is still averaging 5.2 yards per carry on the season and now is up to 983 yards from scrimmage and five total touchdowns heading into next Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Bengals in Madrid.

Terrell didn't play in Week 8 versus the 49ers, his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He practiced in a limited capacity during the week but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation for the divisional meeting with the Buccaneers. However, Terrell now has the green light to return from the one-game layoff, which will likely result in less work for C.J. Henderson (groin) and Mike Ford.

It's an awful situation for Thompson, who had been set for a chance to play in the NFL after being selected by the Falcons in the sixth round of April's draft. Atlanta has not said much about Thompson, who currently resides on the team's reserve/non-football injury list.

injuries.evidence: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season.
injuries.detail: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losing four games in a row.

Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.

Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.

With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

Moody made his only field-goal try and converted his only extra-point attempt during Thursday's 33-10 loss versus the Jaguars. Regular starting kicker Tyler Loop (groin) is not eligible to return from injured reserve until after the Ravens' bye in Week 13, so the team is expected to either sign Moody to its active roster or elevate him again ahead of its Week 10 matchup versus the Chargers.

Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

Additionally, the Cardinals are paying about half of Brissett's remaining 2026 salary to facilitate the deal. The move gives Baltimore a veteran quarterback after both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) suffered long-term injuries last Sunday against Buffalo. Brissett had recently fallen to the Cardinals' No. 3 quarterback after he was benched in Week 8 against Dallas. He should immediately claim the QB1 spot for the Ravens after undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano has looked overmatched in his nearly two full games of action under center.

Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

Hamilton tweaked his hip late in the first half, and after he was able to play through it briefly early in the second half, he has now been ruled out for the rest of the team's Week 9 matchup. The 25-year-old will now shift his focus to being ready for the team's Week 10 contest against the Chargers on Nov. 16. In Hamilton's absence, Keyon Martin is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities in Baltimore's secondary.

Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.

Wiggins is under the weather and initially carried a questionable tag ahead of this contest. However, he won't be out there Thursday, meaning veteran Chidobe Awuzie will presumably take on more snaps at cornerback.

Practice-squad elevation Austin Reed moved up to the No. 2 spot on the depth chart ahead of the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. While Slovis is inactive, he will be available if Reed and starter Joe Fagnano exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.evidence: The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending.
injuries.detail: Huntley and Lamar Jackson (thumb) were both placed on injured reserve Thursday. The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending. Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.

Hawkins was again unable to practice during the week, and he will be sidelined for his third consecutive game in Week 9 as he deals with a nagging knee injury. K'Von Wallace figures to continue to see increased reps in the secondary in Hawkins' stead.

Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.

Anderson didn't practice Thursday or Friday due to an ankle injury, but he was able to log a limited session Saturday to have at least a chance of suiting up Monday. If Anderson ends up being sidelined, Austin Corbett could draw the start at left guard.

Brown missed last Sunday's win over Baltimore, but he'll be back in action Monday after logging an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. His return will be especially critical if fellow starting offensive tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs, questionable) isn't able to suit up.

Dawkins didn't practice at all this week due to an injury to his ribs, but he still has a chance to suit up. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, the veteran tackle was hurt in the first half of last Sunday's win over Baltimore but was able to finish out the contest. Dawkins said he'll do everything he can to be ready for Monday Night Football, so he may be a true game-time decision.

Shavers remains on the reserve/PUP list with a knee injury despite logging three consecutive full practices during Week 9 prep. The wide receiver could return to the active roster ahead of Monday night's showdown with the Vikings, but it will be contingent on the Bills creating a spot on the 53-man roster in time.

Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.

While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.

Palmer exited last Sunday's win against the Ravens in the first half and wasn't able to return due to a hamstring injury. After not practicing Thursday or Friday, the Bills opted to keep him on the sidelines in Week 9, meaning Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and/or Tyrell Shavers (knee, IR) may see WR reps behind the team's top trio at the position.
A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.

Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.

Alford was inactive for Sunday's win over the Ravens, though it appears he will be back on the field when the Bills face the Vikings on Monday night. With the 28-year-old back in the equation, Te'Cory Couch and Maxwell Hairston will likely see fewer snaps.

Hancock has been on IR since late September while recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 versus Detroit. The cornerback had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and if he isn't activated in that time frame, he will remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.

With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.

Bass converted multiple long-range field goals for the Bills after the offense stalled several times due to drops. The kicker succeeded from 56 yards, 22 yards and 51 yards in the contest. Bass has converted all 16 of his field-goal attempts and is 21-for-23 on PATs through seven games this season.

Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.

Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.

Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.

Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.
Simpkins didn't suit up in the Week 8 loss to Green Bay due to an ankle injury, though it won't keep him off the field again for Sunday's meeting with the Broncos.

Sanders is active for the first time this season. He will likely act as a depth piece behind the team's usual starters, Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller, but should he get playing time, he could emerge as a trade candidate at the league's trade deadline Tuesday, Nov. 10.
Bullock was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. However, after logging full sessions Thursday and Friday, he is good to go for Week 9.

It's the third straight week that Dillon is a healthy scratch, and he hasn't logged game-day action since Week 4 against Detroit. Meanwhile, rookie RB Anthony Tyus continues to be active, due largely to his work as a kick returner. As such, it appears Dillon isn't likely to suit up unless one of the RBs ahead of him in the pecking order -- Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne or Tyus -- needs to miss time.

King should be used to this role, as it's one he's had in each of Carolina's contests so far  this season. It has yet to yield a regular-season snap for the rookie out of Georgia Tech, and King will be eligible to enter Sunday's matchup only if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

Christensen has been on injured reserve since Sept. 1. He was designated to return Tuesday and was a full participant in all three of Carolina's practices this week, but the Panthers aren't ready to activate him. Christensen's next chance to play is Sunday, Nov. 15, in New Orleans.

Wilson was elevated for the first time this season last weekend, and he ended up starting and logging every Panthers defensive snap against Green Bay. The veteran cornerback could do the same Sunday versus Denver, as Will Lee has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury and Akayleb Evans (triceps) is on IR. Wilson finished with eight tackles and two defensed passes in his Panthers debut.

Young has been a full practice participant throughout the week, apparently not too bothered by a sore ankle. The bigger concern for Sunday is Denver's impressive pass rush matching up against Carolina's injury-riddled offensive line.

Brown missed last Thursday night's loss to the Packers but appears ready to return for Sunday's Week 9 date with Denver. He has seven tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup across 142 defensive snaps this season.

Wheatley was able to secure a career-high seven stops, while his biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter when he picked off a deep pass from Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The interception was the first of the Wheatley's career, and the rookie has now compiled 26 total tackles (19 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over six contests during the 2026 campaign.

The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.

Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.

Canales noted that Legette still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the third-year wideout appears to have at least progressed on some level since landing on IR on Oct. 3. Before getting hurt, Legette had served as the Panthers' No. 3 wideout during the first two weeks of the season and produced a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets between those contests.

Tremayne took the field for 19 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, with his 26-percent share marking his lowest rate since Week 2. The 26-year-old appears to have been passed up on the depth chart at receiver by John Metchie, who logged 33 snaps Thursday and has now had higher playing-time shares than Tremayne for three straight games.

Metchie took the field for 33 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, placing him behind Tetairoa McMillan (65 snaps) and Jalen Coker (63) but ahead of Brycen Tremayne (19) and David Moore (zero) among Carolina receivers. Though he's now drawn at least three targets in five straight games, Metchie has found the end zone just once and is averaging 22.8 receiving yards per contest during that stretch.

After logging a season-high 13 snaps on offense a week earlier in the Panthers' blowout loss to the Buccaneers, Moore's playing time was contained to special teams while Carolina leaned exclusively on Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie at receiver.

Fitzgerald didn't attempt a kick in the Week 7 loss to Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old got back on the board Thursday, draining a 39-yard field goal early in the first quarter before capping off the night with a 50-yarder late in the third. Fitzgerald has made all 13 of his field goals this season, though he's missed five extra-point attempts.

Coker was having a forgettable night before he used his speed to turn a short Bryce Young pass into a 26-yard touchdown with just under six minutes remaining in the contest. Coker's fumble came on the last play of the game, as he lost the handle on the ball shortly after receiving a lateral from Tetairoa McMillan at the Panthers' 26-yard line. Coker is in the midst of a two-game downturn that unsurprisingly coincides with struggles on the part of Bryce Young, as the speedy wideout has just three receptions for 45 yards and Thursday's score in that span heading into a tough Week 9 assignment at home against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Hubbard was able to log his usual hefty workload despite Carolina trailing for large swaths of the contest, and the veteran back added his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run on the first play of the second quarter. He also led the Panthers in receptions with a season-high figure, and he now has seven total scores in seven games. Hubbard averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the first time this season, but he's still clocking 4.6 yards per tote heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

McMillan led the Panthers in receiving yards despite generating a modest total, and the second-year wideout has now fallen under 60 receiving yards in consecutive games for the first time this season. He does have at least six grabs in three of the past four games and a trio of double-digit target tallies on the season, so he continues to sport a formidable fantasy floor despite Bryce Young's current struggles. Carolina's air attack may have a tough time bouncing back in Week 9, however, as the stingy Broncos defense comes to town on Sunday, Nov. 8.

A thumb injury left Stevenson uncertain for Week 9, and his availability will not officially be revealed until 90 minutes before Sunday's 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. However -- per the report -- with help from a splint, it appears he will be ready to take the field.
Muhammad missed last week's victory over the Seahawks due to a toe injury sustained in Week 7, but it appears he will miss only the lone contest.

Monangai was able to get back on the practice field Friday for the first time since suffering a turf-toe injury versus the Jets on Oct. 4, but his limited showing in that session seemingly won't be enough to clear him to suit up Sunday. The Bears have a Week 10 bye on tap, so it comes as no surprise that the team likely will hold off on Monangai's return for two more weeks. Yet again, D'Andre Swift will pace Chicago's backfield this weekend, with Roschon Johnson also on hand for RB reps.

Ahmed is set to be elevated for the first time since signing with Chicago's practice squad in September. With Zavier Scott (wrist) being placed on injured reserve Thursday and Kyle Monangai dealing with thumb and toe injuries, Ahmed could be called upon to provide additional depth behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson against Tampa Bay.

After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.

injuries.evidence: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games.
injuries.detail: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

injuries.evidence: He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
injuries.detail: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

injuries.evidence: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

When Cole Kmet went to the Bears' injured reserve list with a season-ending knee injury following Week 7, it left the team with just two healthy tight ends on its active roster, so the move gives the club some much-needed depth at the position. As long as starter Colston Loveland and rookie third-rounder Sam Roush remain available, though, Carlson's role will likely be limited as the season progresses.

With Cole Kmet landing on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, Roush stepped into an increased role on offense, as his 53 percent snap share represented a season-best mark. However, the added playing time didn't translate to any involvement in the passing game, as Roush ran just 12 routes on the night. The Bears' frequent usage of two-tight-end formations should continue to prop up Roush's snap counts, but he's likely to be utilized mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.

With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) inactive for a fourth straight game, Johnson continued to serve as the No. 2 running back behind D'Andre Swift. Unsurprisingly, Swift (27 carries for 69 yards and three touchdowns) handled the brunt of the work out of the backfield, with Johnson taking the field for just 14 of the team's 70 offensive snaps. If Monangai is able to make it back for Sunday's matchup with the Buccaneers, Johnson's playing time on offense could disappear entirely.

Santos made 44- and 38-yard field goals in the second quarter. It was a nice bounce-back game for the veteran kicker after he'd missed a field-goal try in each of the previous three games. For the season, Santos is 13-for-17 on FGAs and a perfect 25-for-25 on PATs. Being attached to the Bears offense makes Santos an attractive fantasy kicker.

Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.

Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards on the night while finishing second in receptions and targets. The third-year wideout's catch and yardage totals both qualified as his second highest of the season, and Odunze now has 156 receiving yards over the last pair of contests for his most productive two-game stretch this season. Odunze is averaging a career-best 16.7 yards per catch and already has a career-high 14 receptions of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Loveland continued his upward trajectory by tying Luther Burden for the team lead in catches and targets, and he finished second in receiving yards to Rome Odunze. The second-year tight end's fourth-quarter fumble was costly for the moment, however, as Loveland lost the ball at the Bears' 21-yard line following an eight-yard reception, and the turnover ultimately led to the Seahawks' final touchdown of the contest. Nevertheless, Loveland now has at least six receptions in four of the last five games, including three straight, and he's drawn 21 targets over the last pair of contests alone heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Swift put in a full night's work while repeatedly butting heads with the Seahawks' elite run defense, as his longest run went for only seven yards, and he averaged 2.6 yards per carry overall. He sealed the win for Chicago with his third touchdown of the game, a five-yard run with 4:41 remaining. That score was preceded by one- and five-yard TDs earlier in the second half, and Swift's carry total was a season high. The veteran running back is up to a career-high 10 rushing touchdowns heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Keenum will serve as the No. 3 QB for the third straight week, while Tyson Bagent slots in as the primary backup behind starter Caleb Williams. Keenum will only be eligible to enter the contest if both Williams and Bagent are forced out of the game.

Sanborn was unable to play against the Patriots in Week 7 due to a concussion, but he was a full participant in all three practices of Week 8 prep, and he has cleared the league's protocol after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. He has four tackles (three solo) across six regular-season games while serving mostly on special teams.

It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.

Turner was injured in last Sunday's overtime win against the Titans and was unable to return. He avoided a serious injury and will be ready to do battle with Drake London in Spain on Sunday.

Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

For the second straight week, the Bengals' kicker did not attempt a field goal but connected on all five of his extra-point tries. He's certainly getting scoring attempts in the high-flying Bengals offense, though a few more field-goal tries would boost his fantasy value.

The Bengals were chasing the Titans on the scoreboard much of the afternoon, and Chase Brown and Perine combined for just 16 carries, as Joe Burrow fired off 48 pass attempts. Perine is a touchdown-or-bust desperation RB3 in fantasy whose main value comes in the form of being Brown's backup. Cincinnati has been linked to a potential trade for a running back ahead of next week's deadline.

Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.

Gesicki was able to reach the end zone for the fifth straight game, connecting with Joe Burrow for a 25-yard score in the fourth quarter. The tight end's four catches and 76 receiving yards were both his highest totals since Week 1 versus Tampa Bay. Gesicki has now caught 17 of 24 targets for 241 yards and six scores over seven contests to open the regular season.

Brown led the Bengals in rushing with an efficient performance, and he finished with his best yardage total on the ground since Week 3. Brown's very busy day as a receiver was second only to his 11-catch, 71-yard effort against the Jaguars in Week 4, and his lost fumble, his second of the season, came early in the fourth quarter and led to a Titans touchdown. Brown is in line to fill  his usual voluminous dual role in a Week 9 international matchup against the Falcons in Madrid next Sunday.

Higgins led the Bengals' air attack in receiving yards and touchdown catches on a day when Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdown passes overall. Higgins was responsible for a pair, making 17- and 18-yard scoring grabs in the second half. The latter erased a 36-29 deficit with 1:17 remaining in regulation to help force overtime, and Higgins now has at least 148 receiving yards in three of the last four games and a pair of TD catches in two straight. The veteran has essentially moved into a true 1-A role alongside Ja'Marr Chase in the passing attack, and Higgins will look to carry the massive momentum into a Week 9 matchup against a vulnerable Falcons secondary in Madrid next Sunday.

Chase finally struck for his first 100-yard effort of the campaign in Sunday's wild win, finishing with team-high reception and target totals, as well as runner-up status in receiving yards. Chase was also on the receiving end of one of Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes, corralling the first one of the day from 30 yards out early in the second quarter. Chase has now scored in three straight games, and after season-best totals across all three components of his receiving line Sunday, the All-Pro receiver will head into a Week 9 matchup against the Falcons in Madrid with no shortage of momentum.

Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

Carter didn't play every defensive snap for just the first time this season, but his nine stops were tied with Bryan Cook for most on the Bengals. Carter has logged at least five stops in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 50 tackles (22 solo), including 1.5 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble in 2026.

Mafe got to Tyler Huntley for a six-yard sack midway through the first quarter before splitting another sack with Bryan Cook in the fourth. Mafe has logged at least 1.0 sacks in three consecutive games and is up to 4.5 sacks through six regular-season games, which already surpasses his total from 2025 with Seattle (2.0 sacks across 17 regular-season contests).

Cook and Boye Mafe combined for a split sack on Tyler Huntley midway through the fourth quarter, which was Cook's first sack since his rookie year in 2022. The fifth-year safety is up to 26 tackles (18 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through five regular-season games.

Knight finished third on the team in tackles behind Bryan Cook and Barrett Carter during the victory, in addition to snagging his first interception of the campaign. The 26-year-old continues to have a productive season, as he's now recorded seven or more tackles in five of his six appearances, bringing his total on the campaign to 50 (21 solo).

With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both fully healthy, Meyers played just 20 of 53 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on Joe Burrow's 32 dropbacks. Outside of his 7-82-0 receiving performance in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Meyers has totaled six catches for 59 yards in the other five games.

Burton exited due to a calf injury in the first half and was deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to return to action before halftime. Burton should thus continue to get occasional snaps at fullback while also helping out on special teams.

With Deshaun Watson (concussion) inactive, Green will stay the emergency third option for a different starter-backup duo. Shedeur Sanders is set to start at quarterback, with Dillon Gabriel ready to back him up. Green will only enter the contest if both Sanders and Gabriel exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

Watson, who reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before being deemed limited Friday and subsequently heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' tag. Though Watson has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, the Browns have elected to err on the side of caution with the QB who has compiled a 5-3 record as the team's starter to date. With Watson listed as inactive versus New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start, while Dillon Gabriel will serve as Cleveland's No. 2 signal-caller. Taylen Green is the team's emergency No. 3 QB.

It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

Ryan was signed to the practice squad and then elevated in anticipation of Sunday's contest. The tight end has played in all but one game for the Browns and will continue in his role as the No. 3 tight end, a role that will see him predominantly utilized on special teams.

Williams finished the week with back-to-back limited practices heading into Week 9 against the Saints. Williams has recorded 55 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four forced fumbles in eight games this season.

With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.

Coach Todd Monken said the move is because Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed so much practice time this week. Watson has been one of the worst statistical quarterbacks in the league over the last month, so Sanders could potentially keep the job if he has a good game versus the Saints. Sanders' insertion under center doesn't change the outlook of the offense, as both Watson and Sanders are game-manager types.

Szmyt converted his 31-yard and 32-yard field-goal attempts in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all six of the Browns' points in the divisional loss. Szmyt is now 16-for-18 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-12 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a relatively productive day with 324 passing yards (albeit without a score), but Jeudy was on the receiving end of only one of his passes. The veteran wideout logged his usual amount of playing time, notching a 60 percent offensive snap share to finish third among Cleveland wide receivers. It was the third time this season Jeudy has finished without a catch, but the other two instances were in Weeks 3 and 4, and he had been more involved of late, averaging 3.5 catches and 36.3 receiving yards over his previous four games. With that in mind, he could get back on track in Week 9 against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts this year.

For the fourth time in eight appearances, Corley logged double-digit snaps on offense, but the third-year receiver has yet to draw a target this season. He'll continue to provide most of his value to the Browns as a kickoff returner.

The reception was Wallace's second of the season, after he previously notched a 12-yard grab in a Week 6 win over the Ravens. A key part of the Browns' special-teams coverage units, Wallace continues to handle a limited role on offense while the the team relies primarily on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy to fill out snaps at receiver.

Since posting a 3-74-0 receiving line on seven targets in a Week 5 loss to the Jets, Bond has settled back into a muted role on offense. He's logged single-digit snaps in three straight contests, going without a target in each of those games.

Sampson was out-carried 11 to one by Quinshon Judkins, but the former has carved out a role as the preferred pass-catching back for Cleveland since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Over the last two games, Sampson has turned 11 targets into nine catches for 94 yards while adding seven carries for 52 yards. Sampson will have some PPR fantasy appeal during weeks when the Browns are projected to trail on the scoreboard.

Liufau broke his left forearm in the Cowboys' preseason finale against the Saints and has yet to play in the 2026 regular season. The linebacker is set to make his debut in Sunday's contest after being activated from IR on Saturday.

With Lamb already seeing high volume on a regular basis, Flournoy -- who has been targeted four times in each of his last two games -- could see added opportunities in Week 9, along with Mingo to some degree. To date, Flournoy has compiled a 30/342/2 receiving line on 42 targets in eight games, but he could be worth a lineup look Sunday for those scrambling to find a Pickens pivot.

Porter began Week 9 prep with a full practice session, but he was limited both Thursday and Friday due to the ankle issue. The star cornerback is now set to miss his fifth game of the campaign. Cobie Durant is a prime candidate to start in Porter's place Sunday.

Overshown wasn't able to overcome injuries to his hamstring and back in time to be ready to suit up Sunday. He was limited in practice both Thursday and Friday, so the issues may not cause a long-term absence. Shemar James is likely to start alongside Dee Winters at inside linebacker for the Cowboys on Sunday.

Schoonmaker continues to tend to a groin issue and will miss his second straight game. He did manage a trio of limited practices during the week, so the tight end may be able to play next Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco. Dallas' tight-end corps will consist of Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell in Week 9.

Ferguson left last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals on the Cowboys' first possession and wasn't able to return due to an ankle injury. He was diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain, and while head coach Brian Schottenheimer relayed to Jon Machota of The Athletic on Monday that Ferguson has a chance to play in Week 9, the tight end managed just one limited practice (Friday) and was listed as questionable. Now that Ferguson is confirmed to be active, his workload is unclear with two other TEs (Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell) also available to the offense.

For a second week in a row, Pickens endured practice restrictions due to a hamstring injury, leaving him questionable to suit up in Week 9. On Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site that he was "hopeful" Pickens would be available this weekend, but that didn't come to pass. With Pickens and fellow WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson will compose Dallas' receiving corps.

Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.

Hudson will make his NFL debut if he gets into Sunday's game against the Colts. The SMU product latched on with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in May. Hudson is unlikely to see much action versus Indianapolis, and whether he logs any offensive snaps at all could depend upon whether fellow wideout George Pickens (questionable, hamstring) is able to play.

Mitchell was elevated for the second straight week ahead of Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis. In his 2026 debut last Sunday versus Arizona, the tight end logged a healthy 31 offensive snaps but didn't log a target or touch. How much Mitchell plays in Indianapolis will likely depend on whether Jake Ferguson (ankle) and Luke Schoonmaker (groin) are able to suit up.

Lawrence suffered an ankle injury last Sunday in a loss to Arizona and had already been ruled out for Week 9. The move to IR means he'll need to miss at least three additional games, so the earliest Lawrence can return is Monday, Dec. 7, against Seattle. The Cowboys activated fellow linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) from IR on Saturday to fill Lawrence's roster spot.

Smith upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in consecutive sessions to start Week 9 prep. The star left guard is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest to defend Dak Prescott against the Colts' pass rush.

Locke has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The starting strong safety has played in just three regular-season games so far in 2026, with he logged only three defensive snaps played in Week 2. However he seems to be getting healthy and should therefore be set for a prominent role moving forward.

Downs upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice, clearing the league's concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. The rookie first-rounder is all set to suit up for the contest as the starting slot cornerback and reserve punt returner for the Cowboys.

Winters was limited Wednesday. However, after logging a full session Thursday, all signs are pointing toward his availability for the Week 9 meeting with the Colts. The 2023 No. 216 overall pick has appeared in six games in his first season in Dallas, amassing 35 total tackles (23 solo) and one interception.
The fourth-round rookie has been sidelined since Week 4 and has played a total of five offensive snaps this season.

Thompson is still working his way back from a hamstring injury that forced the team to place him on injured reserve in late September, and he is not ready to return to practice quite yet. In his absence, P.J. Locke (concussion), Malik Hooker and Markquese Bell are poised to continue to operate as the Cowboys' primary safeties.

Dallas wasn't really able to get anything going on the ground in Week 8, totaling just 93 rushing yards on 39 carries. Just like the offense as a whole, Goodson found a bit more success in the passing game, and he posted his best receiving total since back in 2024. As long as starter Javonte Williams remains available, though, Goodson should stay in a change-of-pace role.

Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.

Aubrey missed a 61-yard field goal before halftime in a game that ended with a three-point difference. The kicker converted from 31 yards, 35 yards and 41 yards in the contest as the Cowboys offense ended up stalling after long drives multiple times. Aubrey moves to 15-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 20-for-21 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

Arizona's defense had been plenty exploitable this season, allowing 243.7 yards per game and 17 TDs through the air to opposing QBs heading into Week 8 action. Even with his main skill-position talents available Sunday, though, Prescott didn't crack 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 1. He salvaged his day with his first TD on the ground of the campaign, which supplemented a nine-yard TD connection with WR Ryan Flournoy. Prescott and the Cowboys offense will look to get back on track next Sunday versus an exploitable Colts defense on the road.

Per Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette, Waddle headed to the locker room Sunday after having absorbed a hart hit, leaving  Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims as the Broncos' available WRs. Prior to his exit, Waddle caught his only target for 22 yards.

Coleman has not started in any of the four appearances he has made in his rookie season, but he led Broncos running backs in both snaps and touches each of the last two weeks, and it appears he could get the start over J.K. Dobbins on Sunday. Both players should be involved one way or another, and with RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve, Cody Schrader will be the only other Broncos running back available for Week 9.

Tillman was on the injury report ahead of the Week 9 meeting with Carolina due to a hamstring issue. However, he will avoid his second absence of the 2026 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven games for the Broncos this season, amassing 19 total tackles (10 solo).

Humphrey has appeared in Denver's last four regular-season contests. However, he will be a healthy scratch for the meeting with Carolina, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 11 against the Raiders, following the Broncos' bye.

Hufanga was considered a game-time call for this one. However, he won't suit up for a fourth consecutive contest. Hufanga is seemingly moving in the right direction, so there's a chance he will be back on the field in Week 11, following the Broncos' bye.

The second-year wideout foreshadowed a return to game action this past week by putting in three full practices, which led to his activation from injured reserve Saturday. Bryant still carried a questionable tag heading into Sunday, but with his availability now confirmed, he should be ready to reprise the No. 3 role he filled behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle prior to his Week 4 injury. Bryant saw generally modest volume during his three-plus games to date, posting a 9-133-1 line on 12 targets and adding a 16-yard rush on his one carry.
Ehlinger is officially inactive Sunday, though he will be available if Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

Schrader has been elevated for the second straight week after making his Broncos debut last Sunday against Kansas City. He logged just two offensive snaps and didn't get a touch or target in that game, but he he did rack up 50 yards on two kick returns. Schrader figures to fill a similar role against the Panthers as the No. 3 RB behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

Singleton continued to rack up a vast number of stops -- it was the fifth time this season he's recorded double-digit tackles. The star linebacker also registered a sack for the second straight week, coming up huge when he brought down Patrick Mahomes for a six-yard loss late in the fourth quarter on third down. The next play was a missed Harrison Butker 54-yard field-goal try, which led to Denver pulling off the comeback with a touchdown less than a minute later. Singleton has been an elite IDP asset in fantasy this season, as he leads the NFL by a wide margin with 101 tackles through eight weeks.

Bo Nix targeted 10 different pass catchers on 32 total pass attempts, and it was rookie RB Jonah Coleman who led the team in receiving with a 4-63-0 line on five targets. Engram has just three catches for 15 yards over his last three games and isn't a recommended fantasy bet ahead of Sunday's date with the Panthers.

Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 39 and 45 yards in the first half. Kicking in Denver's anemic offense through eight games, the veteran has made just 14 of 17 FGAs and all 14 PATs. He's not an exciting fantasy kicker despite playing his home games in a kicker-friendly environment.

The block-first tight end secured a two-yard score in the fourth quarter to pull the Broncos within three points, before they scored the eventual game-winning touchdown on the next possession. Adkins now has six grabs for 44 yards and a score on seven targets this season. He has no fantasy appeal.

While the veteran RB got the start, by the end of the game Dobbins had fully given way to rookie Jonah Coleman, who wound up delivering 104 scrimmage yards on 15 touches and scored the game-winning touchdown. With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, Dobbins will still have a role in the Denver backfield, but Coleman made a compelling case Sunday to become the team's new No. 1 back. Dobbins should at least be more productive in Week 9, even on limited volume, against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.

The Broncos were staring at a 24-13 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but late comebacks are nothing new for Nix. The QB hit Nate Adkins for a two-yard score with about nine minutes left before connecting with Jonah Coleman on a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up the game-winning TD plunge by the rookie RB just after the two-minute warning. It's the 15th time that Nix has led Denver on a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime, the most by any quarterback in the first three seasons of his career since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970. While he's thrown multiple TDs just twice in the first eight games of the season, Nix has gone five straight contests without tossing an INT. He'll take a 9:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 road tilt against the Panthers.

Sutton went to the medical tent after taking a hard hit, but the wideout was able to return to action not long after he did so. In the process he'll bolster a Denver Week 9 WR corps that also includes Jaylen Waddle, Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey.

Allen injured his hamstring in Week 7 against the Cardinals, but he's been given the green light to play Sunday after having his reps limited during Week 8 prep. He has 24 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, two pass defenses and one forced fumble through seven regular-season games.

Saylors carried a questionable designation heading into this contest, though he won't be on the field in Week 9, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. With Sione Vaki (ankle) available, Saylors likely wouldn't have been very involved, regardless.

Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.

St. Brown tended to a rib injury during Week 9 prep that limited him in all three sessions and left him questionable ahead of the weekend. Having said that, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Sunday morning that St. Brown was expected to play, which now has been confirmed. St. Brown will be taking on a Dolphins defense that has allowed an NFL-worst 9.8 yards per target to opposing wide receivers this season.

Small signed with the team's practice squad in September and is now set to be elevated for the first time this season. With Sione Vaki (ankle) and Jacob Saylors (neck) both dealing with injuries, Small could be in line to serve as Detroit's No. 2 running back behind Jahmyr Gibbs against Miami.

Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

Joseph was a limited participant throughout Week 9 prep. Despite maintaining consistent practice participation, the free safety will not be activated from the reserve/PUP list for Sunday's game. The Lions will likely wait until Joseph has logged multiple full sessions and is fully ready to return to the field. Chuck Clark will continue to start at free safety opposite Brian Branch.

With consecutive full practices to close out Week 9 prep, Branch has officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. The starting strong safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's game alongside free safety Chuck Clark.
